summary: Critical comparison of six anonymous independent translations (RU, EN) of the Synopsis of music against the Greek; adversarial verification; terminology concordance

leak.summary: Leak review done in three rounds on 31.10.2026 (runs wf_f03ae519-ef8, wf_292a52eb-0e1 and the first); the last found one blocking gap (verifiers' contamination field) and minor issues, all fixed as specified; it stated that no further review round was needed.

units.sense: Title: 'Synopsis of music, made exact'. σύνοψις = a comprehensive survey, compendium; ἠκριβωμένη is the perfect passive participle of ἀκριβόω, 'made exact, worked out with precision'. The word order σύνοψις ἠκριβωμένη is that of cod. H, Par., cod. V (Bas. inverts it).

divergences.issue: Rendering of the title: the noun (обзор / синопсис / обозрение / начертание / изложение в сокращении) and the participle (precise / accurate / accurately worked out).

readings.en: Synopsis of Music, accurately worked out

readings.construal: adjective 'accurate'; Russian noun 'начертание' (an old title-word for a compendium)

divergences.verdict: All are legitimate. The perfect participle states a result ('made exact'), so 'precise' is enough. The Russian noun has to be chosen for the whole series, since every science in the Quadrivium is headed σύνοψις.
evidence: LSJ s.v. ἀκριβόω 'make exact or accurate' [from memory]
divergences.recommended_en: A Precise Synopsis of Music
divergences.recommended_ru: Точный обзор музыки

best_ru.why: Short, exact and idiomatic ('Точный обзор/обозрение музыки'), without padding.

best_en.why: 'A Precise Synopsis of Music' is exact and reads as a title.

notes_to_keep.gist: Music placed directly after arithmetic matches Theon's order of the mathemata, with music 'in numbers' second (Theon 16.24-17.15 Hiller; verified).

editor_questions: Which Russian noun for σύνοψις (обзор / синопсис / обозрение) should be used across all four synopses?

units.sense: The ancients said that music holds the universe together, for nothing that exists is without commensurability and proportion.

divergences.issue: Russian term for ἀναλογία: 'пропорция' versus 'соотношение'.
divergences.verdict: 'Пропорция' is right. In the Platonic tradition behind the passage, ἀναλογία is geometric proportion (Ti. 31c-32c). 'Соотношение' is too weak and collides with λόγος ('отношение') later in the text.
evidence: LSJ s.v. ἀναλογία, 'mathematical proportion', citing Pl. Ti. 31c-32c [from memory]
divergences.recommended_en: commensurability (συμμετρία) and proportion (ἀναλογία)
divergences.recommended_ru: соразмерности (συμμετρία) и пропорции (ἀναλογία)

errors.quote: без соразмерности и соотношения
errors.problem: ἀναλογία is rendered 'соотношение' (also in U003 and U004), which loses the technical sense 'proportion'.

errors.quote: commensurability and proportion
errors.problem: No Greek in parentheses at the first occurrence of συμμετρία and ἀναλογία, as the brief requires.

best_ru.why: Exact, idiomatic, with the Greek terms; A also marks τὸ πᾶν.

best_en.why: Exact and fluent, with the Greek terms.

notes_to_keep.gist: The Pythagoreans in Theon 12.10-13.1 Hiller: the end of music is to unite and fit together; 'in the cosmos harmonia, in the city good order, in houses temperance' (verified).
Plato, Timaeus 31c-32c: the cosmos bound by ἀναλογία.

units.sense: Nor would anything that comes to be ever come to be well if it did not come to be with the fitting commensurability and proportion, whether it is a product of art or of nature, perceptible by sense or contemplated by thought alone.

errors.quote: не возникло бы хорошо
errors.problem: ποτε is left out (the English has 'ever').

errors.quote: Nor could anything that comes to be come to be well / не могло бы возникнуть хорошо
errors.problem: ποτε is left out in both languages.

best_ru.why: Complete (ποτε rendered), with natural syntax for the four κἄν clauses.

best_en.why: Complete and close to the Greek ('ever', 'fitting').

notes_to_keep.gist: Plato, Philebus 64d-e: measure and commensurability (μετριότης καὶ συμμετρία) turn out everywhere to be beauty and excellence.

units.sense: Music is a kind of self-commensurability (commensurability itself) and proportion, [wholly so / the All], inasmuch as it is the harmony of the universe.

divergences.issue: Is τὸ πᾶν, set off by commas, an adverbial accusative ('wholly') or a noun in apposition ('the All')?

readings.en: is wholly a kind of ... proportion / proportion — wholly so
proportion, the whole / — the All itself —

divergences.verdict: The adverbial reading is preferable. The author uses τὸ πᾶν adverbially three times in U055 (οὐ μὴν τὸ πᾶν διὰ τόνων ... οὐδὲ τὸ πᾶν ἐκ διέσεων); with the appositional reading the causal clause ('since it is the harmony of the universe') would be nearly tautological. The appositional reading cannot be excluded, given the play on τὸ πᾶν / τοῦ παντός in U002-U005.
evidence: LSJ s.v. πᾶς, adverbial τὸ πᾶν 'altogether' [from memory]
divergences.recommended_en: Music is a kind of self-commensurability (αὐτοσυμμετρία) and proportion, wholly so, inasmuch as it is the harmony of the universe.
divergences.recommended_ru: Музыка же есть некая самосоразмерность (αὐτοσυμμετρία) и пропорция — всецело, поскольку она есть гармония вселенной.

divergences.issue: The force of οἷα with the participle: causal, or a hedge ('as it were')?

readings.en: inasmuch as it is the harmony of the universe
being, as it were, the harmony of the whole

divergences.verdict: Causal. With a participle, οἷα (like ἅτε) gives the reason as a fact on the writer's authority. 'As it were' turns an identification into a simile.
evidence: Smyth, Greek Grammar §2085 (ἅτε, οἷα, οἷον with the circumstantial participle) [from memory]
divergences.recommended_en: inasmuch as it is the harmony of the universe
divergences.recommended_ru: поскольку она есть гармония вселенной

divergences.issue: 'Commensurability itself' versus 'self-commensurability'.

readings.ru: сама соразмерность / соразмерность сама по себе

divergences.verdict: Both are legitimate. The word has no entry in LSJ, DGE or the other Logeion lexica. Whichever form is chosen, the Greek should be given and the formation explained in a note.
evidence: Logeion (LSJ, DGE, Bailly, Pape): no entry for αὐτοσυμμετρία [checked]

errors.quote: being, as it were, the harmony of the whole / будучи как бы гармонией целого
errors.problem: The causal οἷα + participle is turned into a hedge ('as it were'), so the identification of music with the harmony of the All becomes a mere comparison.
errors.fix: inasmuch as it is the harmony of the universe / поскольку она есть гармония вселенной

errors.quote: — the All itself — / — само всё —
errors.problem: 'Itself' has no Greek counterpart (τὸ πᾶν, not αὐτὸ τὸ πᾶν).

errors.quote: и пропорция вообще
errors.problem: 'Вообще' means 'in general' and makes the phrase 'proportion in general' instead of 'wholly'.

errors.quote: Музыка же в целом есть
errors.problem: 'В целом' ('on the whole') hedges the claim and attaches it to music; the English has 'altogether'.

best_ru.why: Clear adverbial construal ('— всецело,'), correct causal clause, Greek terms given.

best_en.why: Correct causal clause, adverbial τὸ πᾶν, and a doubt that argues the alternative.

notes_to_keep.gist: αὐτοσυμμετρία is unrecorded in LSJ, DGE, Bailly and Pape (confirmed: no Logeion entry); it is formed like the Platonic αὐτο- compounds: music is commensurability itself, not a commensurate thing.
Doubt: τὸ πᾶν is adverbial, as in U055; the alternative 'the All' is given in both languages.

editor_questions: τὸ πᾶν: adverbial ('wholly'; recommended) or 'the All' in apposition? Print the other reading in a note.
αὐτοσυμμετρία: 'commensurability itself' or 'self-commensurability' (самосоразмерность)?

units.sense: Perhaps one might, not unreasonably, call even the Divine itself the harmony both of itself and of the universe: in it [the Divine] the universe, fitted together and joined, is clearly seen to be in a good, indeed the best possible, state.

divergences.issue: Antecedent of the relative: τὸ θεῖον (neuter) or ἁρμονίαν (feminine)?

readings.en: the harmony of itself and of the All — that in which the All ...

divergences.verdict: Τὸ θεῖον. ᾧ cannot agree with the feminine ἁρμονίαν, which would require ᾗ. The Pauline model (Eph. 2:21 ἐν ᾧ; 4:16 ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα συναρμολογούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον) also places the joining of the whole in God or Christ.
evidence: Greek agreement (relative in gender with its antecedent), Smyth §2501 [from memory]
divergences.recommended_en: in which [the Divine] the universe, being fitted together and joined, is clearly seen to be in a good, indeed the best possible, state
divergences.recommended_ru: в нём вселенная, слаживаемая и согласуемая, явно пребывает в добром и наилучшем состоянии

errors.quote: той, в которой всё ... / that in which the All ...
errors.problem: The relative is attached to the feminine 'harmony' against the gender of ᾧ, so the clause no longer says that the universe is held together in the Divine.
errors.fix: в нём (в божественном) всё ... / in which [the Divine] the All ...

best_ru.why: E: correct antecedent, clear syntax, the Pauline participles marked. A: deliberate echo of the Synodal Eph. 4:16, explained in a note.

best_en.why: Exact, with 'clearly seen' for διαφαίνεται and correct reference of ἐν ᾧ.

notes_to_keep.gist: συναρμολογούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον is almost verbatim Eph. 4:16 (cf. 2:21, Col. 2:19); LSJ gives only these places. The Russian «составляемое и совокупляемое» deliberately follows the Synodal version (verified: the Synodal Eph. 4:16 reads «составляемое и совокупляемое»). A also remarks on the future optative ὀνομάσοι with ἄν.
Eph. 2:21 has exactly ἐν ᾧ ... συναρμολογουμένη; ἐν ᾧ here refers to τὸ θεῖον (neuter), not to ἁρμονία; the compiler Christianizes the Pythagorean commonplace.

units.sense: Of so great a wonder did they deem music worthy.

best_ru.why: 'Сочли ... достойной' renders ἠξίωσαν exactly.

best_en.why: Literal and natural ('Of so great a wonder did they deem music worthy').

units.sense: Music being thus contemplated in all things, governing and ordering all things, and granting pleasure to sense, harmony to nature and blessedness to intellect, we shall treat in summary of music in sense-perception, or rather of the music contemplated in one of the senses, hearing.

divergences.greek: ἧς ἐν ἅπασιν οὕτω θεωρουμένης ... χαριζομένης
divergences.issue: What does the genitive absolute express: cause or concession?

readings.en: Since it is thus observed/contemplated in all things ...
readings.ru: Поскольку она так наблюдается / созерцается во всём ...

readings.en: (Thus,) although/though it is observed in all things ...

divergences.verdict: Both are legitimate. The Greek states no relation (there is no καίπερ), and the circumstantial participle takes its force from the context. The concessive reading fits the narrowing μᾶλλον δέ; the causal reading fits οὕτω, which looks back to the encomium.
evidence: Smyth §§2060-2070 (circumstantial participle; the relation is inferred from the context) [from memory]
divergences.recommended_en: Since music is thus contemplated in all things ..., we shall treat in summary of music in sense-perception
divergences.recommended_ru: Поскольку музыка так созерцается во всём ..., мы вкратце рассмотрим музыку в чувственном восприятии

divergences.issue: Sense of διέπω (and κοσμέω).
divergences.verdict: 'Govern'. LSJ gives 'manage, conduct'; the prose example is Arist. Mu. 399a18, God governing the cosmos. The only motion-sense is 'traverse', and that only in poetry (AP). For κοσμέω, 'order' (A, B, D, E, F) suits the cosmological pair better than C's 'adorn', but 'adorn' is not wrong.
divergences.recommended_en: governs and orders all things
divergences.recommended_ru: всем управляет и всё упорядочивает

errors.quote: pervades / всё пронизывает
errors.problem: διέπω means 'govern, manage' (LSJ); 'pervade' is not attested for it.

best_ru.why: Exact and complete, with the Greek for αἴσθησις and νόησις.

best_en.why: Accurate rendering of every member; correct 'governs and orders'.

notes_to_keep.gist: Model: Theon 46.20-47.10 Hiller. Consonance 'in reasoning is truth, in life happiness, in nature harmony'; then harmonia that is perceptible (in instruments), intelligible (in numbers) and cosmic (verified).
Theon's division of music into music 'in instruments', 'in numbers' and 'in the cosmos' (Theon 16.24-17.8 Hiller, verified); ἧς is a connecting relative.

editor_questions: Genitive absolute: causal (since) or concessive (although)? Both are defensible; choose one and note the other.

units.sense: A note is the pitch (literally 'tension'), fit for harmony, of a voice without extension.

divergences.issue: 'Tension' (literal, physical) or 'pitch' (the technical sense in definitions of the note)?
divergences.verdict: Both are legitimate. In definitions of the note, τάσις is the stationary pitch-level (LSJ s.v. τάσις 3, 'pitch of the voice'; Cleonides 2 calls the stationary points of the voice τάσεις, a name taken from stretched strings). The author also uses the physical sense (U037, U049). The editor decides the rendering for the whole text; 'pitch' gives the sense, 'tension' keeps the image.
evidence: Cleonides 2, Jan 180.16-181.9: τὰς μὲν οὖν μονὰς τάσεις καλοῦμεν ...; τάσεις μὲν ἀπὸ τῶν καθαπτῶν ὀργάνων παρὰ τὸ τετάσθαι [checked]
Nicomachus, Ench. 4, Jan 242.21-243.2: φθόγγον δὲ φωνῆς ἐμμελοῦς ἀπλατῆ τάσιν· τάσιν δὲ μονήν τινα καὶ ταὐτότητα κατὰ μέγεθος φθόγγου ἀδιαστάτου [checked]
divergences.recommended_en: A note (φθόγγος) is the pitch (τάσις), fit for harmony (ἐναρμόνιος), of a voice without extension (ἀδιάστατος).
divergences.recommended_ru: Звук (φθόγγος) есть пригодная для гармонии (ἐναρμόνιος) высота (τάσις) голоса, не имеющего протяжённости (ἀδιάστατος).

divergences.issue: Rendering of the adjective (not the enharmonic genus).
divergences.verdict: 'Fit for harmony' best matches the author's own gloss in U012 (uttered so as to be able to be fitted with another note). 'Harmonious' is acceptable but may suggest 'pleasant'. 'Harmonically adjusted' implies an adjustment already made.
evidence: LSJ s.v. ἐναρμόνιος I 'in harmony with' vs II 'enharmonic' [from memory]
divergences.recommended_en: fit for harmony (ἐναρμόνιος)
divergences.recommended_ru: пригодная для гармонии (ἐναρμόνιος)

errors.quote: φθόγγος ἐστὶ φωνῆς ἐμμελοῦς τάσις ἐπὶ μίαν πτῶσιν
errors.problem: Misquotes Cleonides 1 with τάσις and πτῶσις swapped, and the doctrine field repeats the error. The text (Jan 179.9-10) is: Φθόγγος μὲν οὖν ἐστι φωνῆς πτῶσις ἐμμελὴς ἐπὶ μίαν τάσιν.
errors.fix: Quote Cleonides correctly: φωνῆς πτῶσις ἐμμελὴς ἐπὶ μίαν τάσιν, 'the incidence of a melodious voice on one pitch'.

errors.quote: Nicomachean: φθόγγος ... ἀπλατῆ τάσιν ... φθόγγου ἀδιαστάτου (Ench. 2, Jan 243.1-3)
errors.problem: The passage is in Ench. 4 (Jan 242.20-243.2), not Ench. 2; the doctrine field repeats 'Ench. 2'.

errors.quote: of an voice without extension
errors.problem: Typo.

errors.quote: A note (phthongos)
errors.problem: The English gives a transliteration where the brief requires the Greek term.

best_ru.why: Exact syntax (ἀδιαστάτου agreeing with φωνῆς), every Greek term given, 'пригодная для гармонии высота'.

best_en.why: Precise rendering with every Greek term; 'pitch ... fit for harmony' reflects the technical sense.

notes_to_keep.gist: Source: Thrasyllus in Theon 47.18-19 Hiller (φωνῆς ἐναρμονίου τάσις); the compiler moves ἐναρμόνιος from the voice to the pitch and takes ἀδιάστατος from Nicomachus, Ench. 4. Cleonides 1 defines the note differently (verified).
ἀδιάστατος means no extension in pitch, not in duration; the next unit compares the note to a geometrical point.
Cleonides 2 calls the stationary points of the voice τάσεις and the passages between them intervals (verified; correct the Nicomachus chapter to Ench. 4).

editor_questions: τάσις: 'pitch / высота' or 'tension / напряжение' throughout the text (cf. U037, U049)?
ἐναρμόνιος: 'fit for harmony' (recommended) or 'harmonious'?

units.sense: An interval is the relation, of a certain kind, of notes to one another.

divergences.issue: Sense of ποιά: 'a certain, determinate' or 'qualitative'?
divergences.verdict: 'A certain (determinate) relation'. In these definitional formulas ποιός marks a relation of a definite kind (the same formula is Thrasyllus', Theon 48.8-9). For Nicomachus the σχέσις of an interval is a λόγος, a measuring ratio, so it is quantitative. 'Qualitative' brings in the Aristotelian category of quality and misleads.
evidence: Theon 48.8-9 Hiller: διάστημα δέ φησιν εἶναι φθόγγων τὴν πρὸς ἀλλήλους ποιὰν σχέσιν [checked]
Nicomachus, Ench. 12, Jan 261: σχέσις δὲ λόγος ἐν ἑκάστῳ διαστήματι μετρητικὸς τῆς ἀποστάσεως [checked]
Cleonides 1, Jan 180.1: γένος ... ποιὰ τεττάρων φθόγγων διαίρεσις [checked]
divergences.recommended_en: An interval (διάστημα) is a certain relation (σχέσις) of notes to one another.
divergences.recommended_ru: Интервал (διάστημα) — некое определённое отношение (σχέσις) звуков друг к другу.

errors.quote: a certain qualitative relation / некое качественное отношение
errors.problem: ποιά is rendered as a category of quality; it means a relation of a determinate kind, and the σχέσις of an interval is a ratio.
errors.fix: a certain relation / некое определённое отношение

errors.quote: Cleonides ch. 2 (von Jan p. 182)
errors.problem: Wrong place: the definition of the interval is Cleonides 1, Jan 179.11-12.

best_ru.why: Exact, with σχέσις marked.

best_en.why: Exact, with the Greek terms.

notes_to_keep.gist: U009-U011 reproduce Thrasyllus' definitions in Theon 48.8-13 Hiller (διάστημα ... ποιὰν σχέσιν; σύστημα ... ποιὰν περιοχήν; ἁρμονία ... συστημάτων σύνταξις) (verified).

units.sense: A system is a certain compass of intervals.

divergences.issue: Rendering of περιοχή (and ποιά again).
divergences.verdict: 'Compass / охват' keeps the idea of comprising within bounds, as in Thrasyllus. 'Collection / совокупность' is acceptable but loses that idea. C's 'объятие' ('hug') is not idiomatic Russian for this.
evidence: Theon 48.10-12 Hiller: σύστημα δὲ διαστημάτων ποιὰν περιοχήν, οἷον τετράχορδον, πεντάχορδον, ὀκτάχορδον [checked]
divergences.recommended_en: A system (σύστημα) is a certain compass (περιοχή) of intervals.
divergences.recommended_ru: Система (σύστημα) — некий определённый охват (περιοχή) интервалов.

errors.quote: некое качественное объятие интервалов
errors.problem: 'Объятие' ('embrace, hug') is unidiomatic and misleading for περιοχή, and 'качественное' repeats the ποιά error.

errors.quote: Cleonides ch. 8 (von Jan p. 200): a system is composed of more than two intervals
errors.problem: False. Cleonides 1 (Jan 180.2) defines the system as composed of more than one interval (τὸ ἐκ πλειόνων ἢ ἑνὸς διαστημάτων συγκείμενον); I found no 'more than two' in the chapter on systems.
errors.fix: Cleonides 1, Jan 180.2: 'composed of more than one interval'.

errors.quote: Cleonides, "what is composed of several intervals or of one" (Cleonid. 1, Jan 180.2)
errors.problem: Misconstrues πλειόνων ἢ ἑνός, where ἤ means 'than': Cleonides requires more than one interval, so the note falsely says a single interval can be a system.
errors.fix: 'what is composed of more than one interval'.

best_ru.why: 'Охват (περιοχή)' is exact and idiomatic.

best_en.why: 'Compass (περιοχή)' is the apt term.

notes_to_keep.gist: Thrasyllus' examples (tetrachord, pentachord, octachord) come back in U051 with the sixteen-chord added; Bas.'s misprint περωχή is corrected from cod. H, Par., cod. V.
Cleonides' definition expressly requires more than one interval; this definition is less specific (verified).

units.sense: Harmonia (attunement) is an ordered arrangement of systems.

divergences.issue: 'Harmony' versus the technical transliteration 'harmonia'.

readings.construal: 'Harmonia' in English, marking the technical sense

divergences.verdict: Both are defensible. In the definition, ἁρμονία is technical: Thrasyllus' examples are Lydian, Phrygian, Dorian, which the author takes up in U065. 'Harmony' keeps the play with the cosmic harmony of U004-U005 and needs a note; 'harmonia' signals the technical sense.
evidence: Theon 48.12-13 Hiller: ἁρμονία δέ ἐστι συστημάτων σύνταξις, οἷον Λύδιος, Φρύγιος, Δώριος [checked]

errors.quote: Гармония же — соединение систем.
errors.problem: 'Соединение' ('combination') drops the ordering in σύνταξις, and the English has 'arrangement'.

best_ru.why: Exact, with the Greek terms; 'упорядочение / расположение (σύνταξις)'.

best_en.why: Exact, with the Greek terms and a note on the technical sense.

notes_to_keep.gist: ἁρμονία here is technical, an attunement made of systems; Thrasyllus' examples Lydian, Phrygian, Dorian come back in U065 in the same order; cf. U053 (verified).
The author uses ἁρμονία both for cosmic harmony (U004-U005) and for this 'arrangement of systems'; in U053 and U061 harmony 'arranges' (συντάττει) systems by genus.

editor_questions: ἁρμονία in the technical definition: 'harmony' with a note, or 'harmonia'?

units.sense: The note, then, is without extension, like the point in geometry; it is called ἐναρμόνιος because it has been uttered so as to be able to be fitted in harmony with another note as well.

errors.quote: The comparison of the note with the geometrical point is the author's own
errors.problem: False. Nicomachus, Exc. 6 (Jan 276.13-277.2) says that the φθόγγος is 'in number the unit, in geometry the point (σημεῖον), in letters the element'.
errors.fix: Cite Nicomachus, Exc. 6 (Jan 276.13-277.2) as a parallel; drop 'the author's own'.

best_ru.why: Exact and keeps the play ἐναρμόνιος / ἐναρμοσθῆναι («гармоничным» ... «приведён в гармонию»), with the perfect rendered.

best_en.why: Exact (perfect 'has been uttered', 'also'), with the wordplay kept.

notes_to_keep.gist: The note-point (and unit, letter) analogy is in Nicomachus, Ench. 12 (φωνὴ ἄτομος, οἷον μονὰς κατ' ἀκοήν) and Exc. 6. Thrasyllus explains ἐναρμόνιος differently (a note that can be found higher than a high one and lower than a low one, Theon 47.19-48.7) (verified).
'Can be fitted together' does not mean consonance: dissonant steps also belong to a system (cf. U038).

units.sense: For if it were not uttered so, it is a discordant note, not ἐναρμόνιος; nor would it be called a note at all, but a noise uttered at random (otherwise than it should be) and of no use for harmony.

divergences.issue: Sense of ἄλλως: 'otherwise', 'at random / amiss', or 'merely'?
divergences.verdict: LSJ II.3 gives 'otherwise than should be, at random, without aim', which suits a participle describing a noise and also covers the contrast with οὕτως. 'At random / amiss' is the best rendering; 'otherwise' is possible but flat. 'Merely' (LSJ: with substantives) suits a participle less well.
divergences.recommended_en: but a noise uttered at random (amiss) and of no use for harmony
divergences.recommended_ru: а лишь неким шумом, произнесённым как попало и непригодным для гармонии

errors.quote: it is a out-of-tune (ἀπηχής) note
errors.problem: Typo (wrong article).

errors.quote: The contrast phthóngos / psóphos is standard: Cleonides 1 (von Jan p. 180)

units.sense: Notes have various names, [the notes] taking their names from their progression and order from low to high: proslambanomenos, hypate hypaton, parhypate hypaton, hypate diatonos, hypate meson, parhypate meson, ⟨meson diatonos⟩, mese simply, paramesos, trite diezeugmene, diatonos diezeugmene, nete diezeugmene, trite hyperbolaion, diatonos hyperbolaion, nete hyperbolaion: the fifteen notes of the Greater Perfect System, two octaves in the diatonic, without the synemmenon tetrachord.

divergences.greek: τρίτη διεζευγμένη, διάτονος διεζευγμένη, νήτη διεζευγμένη; παράμεσος; ὑπάτη διάτονος

units.sense: Of the intervals the smallest is the diesis; next the semitone, which has toward the high a double increase of the diesis; next the tone, which has the semitone doubled and stands at the epogdoic ratio, as nine to eight; so that the semitone is as much as eight and a half and the diesis as much as eight and a quarter [measured against eight]. In fact these are an arithmetical division of 9:8 (17:16, 33:32), not equal halves and quarters.

notes_to_keep.gist: The tone 9:8 is divided arithmetically, 8 - 8 1/4 - 8 1/2 - 9 (17:16, 33:32). The doubling is true only of the excesses, not of the ratios. Against this stand Theon 53.8-16 Hiller ('the semitone is not half a tone, as Aristoxenus thinks'; 9 cannot be divided into equals) and Sectio canonis 16 (all verified).
Cents: tone 203.910, true half 101.955, true quarter 50.978; 17:16 = 104.955, 33:32 = 53.273 (formula 1200 log2 r).

The ladder diesis-semitone-tone is Aristoxenian (Theon 55.11-13: the diesis is a quarter of the tone, half of the semitone); Cleonides 5 (Jan 187.17-18) lists diesis, semitone, tone, ditone below the fourth (verified).

notes_to_keep.gist: The analogy limps. The side of the square of half (double) area is a mean proportional (Euclid VI.13), so a geometric division of the tone would give √72 ≈ 8.485 against 8, not the 8 1/2 of U018. Geometry justifies an equal division in size, not the compiler's arithmetic numbers.
Constructing geometric means could divide the ratio equally, but the author does not construct them and does not remove the error of U018.

by_translator.strengths: The most complete and accurate translations in both languages, with Greek terms at first occurrence and the edition's signs kept. Its references are verified and the best in the group: Thrasyllus in Theon 47-48 as the source of U008-U011; the cod. A diagram in Hiller's Theon, the decisive parallel for U014 and ⟨μέσων διάτονος⟩; Eph. 4:16 with the Synodal echo (verified); Theon 50 on noise and note. Its doubts are well argued (τὸ πᾶν adverbial with U055 evidence, ἐν ᾧ, ἄλλως, νευράν / μοῖραν). It is the only translator to render ὑποτεμεῖν as 'cut down'.
by_translator.weaknesses: Some false or wrong note-claims: Nicomachus 'Ench. 2' for Ench. 4; Cleonides' system definition misconstrued ('several or one'); the note-point comparison called the author's own (it is in Nicomachus, Exc. 6). The literal 'sixteenth number' / 'ninth number' needs its note. The note diagram in U016 uses normalized names unlike A's own translation.

by_translator.strengths: Accurate, plain, readable translations, with Greek for the main terms and correct construals in the hard places (ἐν ᾧ, οἷα, U018 numbers). Sound remarks on arithmetic versus geometric division.
by_translator.weaknesses: Thin and generic doctrine fields and few notes; a doubt in U004 offers no alternative. Omissions of ποτε (U003); Russian normalizes the note names, so ru and en disagree (U014); 'соединение' for σύνταξις; an ambiguous Russian construction in U024; a typo ('an voice').

by_translator.strengths: Fluent prose. A good instinct to mark the technical 'Harmonia' (U011). A clear string-division reading of 8 1/2 and 8 1/4 in U018 checks.
by_translator.weaknesses: The weakest in this group. It makes three sense errors: U004 οἷα read as 'as it were'; U005 relative referred to 'harmony'; U024 'describing a square upon it'. Many references from memory are false or misplaced: Cleonides' definition of the note misquoted, Cleonides chapters and pages wrong, 'more than two intervals', Sectio canonis 'prop. 17', Nicomachus 'Ench. 5'. Misleading terms ('качественное отношение / объятие', 'соотношение' for ἀναλογία). The English lacks Greek terms, the note names are normalized, and the text_issue for Xylander's order is refuted by the parallels.

by_translator.strengths: Rigorous arithmetic and precise checks (cents with the formula, ratio comparisons). Careful handling of the note names, with Greek and the transmitted forms. Correct references to Cleonides 4 (Jan 182) and Sectio canonis 3 and 16 (Jan 152-153, 161). Useful clarifications (ἀδιάστατος in pitch, not duration; 'two' squares).
by_translator.weaknesses: Heavy descriptive Russian for ἐπόγδοος, and in U020 a Russian rendering that fixes an interpretation of ἡμιεπόγδοος. 'Вообще' for τὸ πᾶν (U004). Unidiomatic 'делится до / subdivided to'. Few notes on sources and doctrine.

by_translator.strengths: The best commentary. Its sources are identified and verified: Thrasyllus in Theon; Nicomachus Ench. 4, 11, 12 and Exc. 6; Theon 12-13, 16-17, 19-20, 53; Euclid I.3; Eph. 2:21 and 4:16. It makes the key doctrinal observation (U025) that the geometric analogy implies a mean proportional (√72), not 8 1/2. Excellent doubts (τὸ πᾶν, ὑπάτη διάτονος, μοῖραν) and good scholarly Russian.
by_translator.weaknesses: 'Pervades' for διέπω; 'eight cannot be squared' in English; 'fixed / movable' labels misused in the U014 diagram; no Greek for the note names in the U014 translation; it leans toward Xylander's order of the supplement against the parallels.

by_translator.strengths: Precise, consistent translations with Greek terms. Careful arithmetic (Pythagorean ratios for all fifteen notes) and sensible doubts (U023 'two squares', ταύτην). Correct construals throughout.
by_translator.weaknesses: Few source notes, and evidence fields often boilerplate. Hedging 'в целом' in U004; 'is divisible' for τέμνεται (U019); unidiomatic 'divided / subdivided to'; typos ('a out-of-tune').

overall.summary:
All six translators render this group (the proem, definitions, note names, the smallest intervals and the geometry excursus) competently. No unit or edition sign is lost, and all correctly read 8 1/2 and 8 1/4 as mixed numbers and reject Xylander. The real disputes are few:

- τὸ πᾶν in U004: adverbial is preferred.
- the genitive absolute in U007: causal or concessive, both defensible.
- τάσις in U008: 'pitch' or 'tension', a whole-text choice.
- ἄλλως in U013: 'at random', per LSJ II.3.
- note names in U014: keep the transmitted forms; keep the printed order of the supplement ⟨μέσων διάτονος⟩, which is confirmed by Theon's cod. A diagram and Nicomachus, Ench. 12.
- U020: ὑποτεμεῖν means 'cut down' rather than 'subdivide'; cod. H's μοῖραν is for the editor.
- περιθείς in U024: 'around', not 'upon'.

Translator C makes three sense errors (U004, U005, U024) and several false references. Translators A and E are the best bases in both languages, with D for the Russian of U014 and D or F if 'pitch' is chosen in U008.

Verified findings worth adding to the commentary: U008-U011 follow Thrasyllus in Theon 47.18-48.13; the U014 list matches the diagram in Theon's cod. A; U015-U016 parallel Nicomachus, Ench. 11 (Jan 258); U019 answers Adrastus in Theon 66.1-3 and 66.14-20 (ἡ μονὰς οὐ τέμνεται).

verify.summary:
The first review holds up well. Every quoted error exists, and the main divergence verdicts are supported by the sources I opened: τὸ πᾶν adverbial; οἷα causal (Smyth §2085); ἐν ᾧ referring to τὸ θεῖον; διέπω 'govern'; περιθείς 'around'; the mixed numbers 8 1/2 and 8 1/4.

Corrections for the editor:
1. Wrong page: the Theon passages cited as '66.1-3, 66.5-6, 66.14-20' are at Theon 70.1-3, 70.5-6, 70.14-19 Hiller. This affects the U018 and U020 evidence and the U019 editor question.
2. LSJ s.v. ὑποτέμνω has no 'cut short' or 'subdivide'. The U020 choice between 'cut down' and 'subdivide' is interpretive either way.
3. LSJ records αὐτοσύμμετρος, 'ideally symmetrical'. This favours 'commensurability itself' over 'self-commensurability' in U004.

5. In U013, LSJ ἄλλως II.1 supports 'otherwise' as fully legitimate.

Severities: I lower three to minor (translator C's relative in U005; translator A's notes in U010 and U012). I keep major for translator C's οἷα in U004, the square construction in U024, and the false Cleonides citations in U008 and U010.

divergences.verdict: LSJ s.v. ῥυθμός gives I 'measured motion' (Pl. Lg. 665a ἡ τῆς κινήσεως τάξις), II 'measure, proportion, symmetry of parts', III 'arrangement, order', VI 'manner' [checked]; Pape and Bailly likewise [checked]. Temporal rhythm sets no limit to the size of an interval, and the 'what follows' (U056-U060) shows the limits set by the structure of the tetrachord. The broad sense ('order, proportion') is the likelier, but the literal 'rhythm' keeps the ambiguity. Keep the Greek in parentheses and add a note. A's 'course of the exposition' has no support in the lexica.

notes_to_keep.gist: Cleonides 5 (Jan pp. 187-189): an interval is incomposite if bounded by successive notes; the trihemitone is incomposite only in the chromatic, the ditone only in the enharmonic, and everything above the ditone is composite. The Anonymous' list (with the tritone) and his criterion (fusion, U027) differ. Verified.
Gaudentius 4: an interval is incomposite when no note melodically admissible in that genus can be sung between its bounds. Verified in Jan.

divergences.verdict: The author defines the names here: the fourth taken again after the octave, i.e. octave + fourth (U037 pairs 11-4, 12-5; U039-U041 give 8½ and 9½ tones, 8:3, 3:1). In the classical theorists δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων is two fourths (16:9), dissonant (Sect. can. 11, Jan pp. 158-159 [checked]). Theon uses διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ τεσσάρων for 8:3 (p. 52.4; 56.12-15 H [checked]), as does Cleonides 8 (Jan p. 194 [checked]). 'Double fourth' alone therefore misleads. Render as a name with the Greek and a note. The choice applies to U035-U042 and is the editor's.
divergences.recommended_en: 'twice-fourth' (δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων), 'twice-fifth' (δὶς διὰ πέντε) and 'twice-octave' (δὶς διὰ πασῶν) [note: = octave + fourth 8:3, octave + fifth 3:1, double octave 4:1]
divergences.recommended_ru: «дважды кварта» (δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων), «дважды квинта» (δὶς διὰ πέντε) и «дважды октава» (δὶς διὰ πασῶν) [примеч.: = октава с квартой 8:3, октава с квинтой 3:1, двойная октава 4:1]

divergences.verdict: All render the sense. The parallel is Thrasyllus in Theon p. 48.16-20 H: σύμφωνα κατ’ ἀντίφωνον are the octave and double octave, κατὰ παράφωνον the fifth and fourth [checked]. This is not Gaudentius' sense (c. 8: παράφωνοι lie between consonance and dissonance, the tritone and ditone [checked in Jan; LSJ s.v. παράφωνος checked]). For ἀντίφωνον = octave see [Arist.] Probl. 19.39 (Jan p. 100) [checked]. The author's antiphonic 11th and 12th are explained by U037's octave pairs (11-4, 12-5), as in A's doubt.

by_translator.strengths: Accurate construal throughout. Its references were checked and are right (LSJ σύμφθαρσις/συμφθείρω/ἄρρευστος/ἀνεγχώρητος; Theon 48 and 51 H; Problems 19.39). It has the best handling of U035 ('repeated', δίς names marked as names, sound doubt explaining the antiphonic 11th/12th), and a valuable note on the P passage as a variant recension of U019-U025.
by_translator.weaknesses: Uses non-standard English 'uncomposite'. Russian «шестнадцатое число» reads as a date. Some calques («в непрерывности»). Proposes an unnecessary normalisation αὐτῇ in U031.

by_translator.strengths: Clean, natural, generally accurate Russian and English. Correct construals in the hard places (U027 'spanning', U031, U035 syntax). Sensible brief notes on the δίς names and the two-square restriction.
by_translator.weaknesses: Thin on notes and parallels. Greek missing at first occurrences (ἀσύνθετα, ἄμεσα) and where the etymology turns on the names (U034). Small slips: causal «поскольку» (U026), «проходит» for τελούμενον, «согласуются» for συμφωνεῖ.

by_translator.strengths: Literal and consistent terminology ('through four'). Correct textual judgments on ἑξκαιδέκατον and on keeping the δίς names. Useful doubt on τὸ παρὰ μίαν.
by_translator.weaknesses: Several major errors. σύμφθαρσις becomes 'compression', with a false pyknon doctrine. «воздаваясь» for ἀπηχούμενον. A false claim that U027's word is a conjecture. Wrong construals in U031 ('describing it as a square') and U035 (subject and predicate inverted). False or unverifiable notes (Cleonides 12 / Gaudentius 4 on paraphony; Cleonides 3 on ἄμεσα; Tsypin via about.md). Russian slips («о интервалах», «названность», «созвучат», «триполутоние»). Not usable as a base.

by_translator.strengths: Careful, sober and accurate. Verified references (Cleonides 5 and 8, Gaudentius 4). Good arithmetic checks. Correct treatment of the conjectures in P. Clear statement of the δίς referents without emending.
by_translator.weaknesses: Sometimes explanatory rather than terminological (ἄμεσα as 'intervals without intermediate notes', «интервальные расстояния»). «напев» for μέλος. A minor omission in U030 ru. 'Double fourth' without a literal gloss.

by_translator.strengths: The most thorough and exact. Lexicon and parallels verified (LSJ, Pape, DGE; Theon 48, 51, 54, 56 H; Sect. can. 11; Gaudentius 8; Problems 19.39). Well-argued doubt on ῥυθμός. Precise ἐγγίνεται 'it is possible'. Best renderings in U027, U028, U034, U036.
by_translator.weaknesses: 'eight cannot be squared' (misleading English). The textual note on τῆς is misplaced in U028. Leans on Jan's editorial note on Bacchius (a trap area). Uses the transliterated 'melos/melē'. 'Double fourth' as the main rendering (with a gloss).

by_translator.strengths: Generally accurate and complete. Good Russian in U028-U031. Correct checks. Sound remarks on the two-square restriction and on ratios multiplying.
by_translator.weaknesses: U035 renders διὰ πασῶν as 'octave' and so loses the etymology (major). Flattens the three verbs in U034. Misjudges the δίς labels as 'irregular' and favours Xylander's reading on a false premise (U036). 'Different tones' for διαφόρων τόνων.

overall.summary: Group 2 (U026-U036) covers the incomposite intervals and 'fusion' (σύμφθαρσις), the P-only passage U028-U032 (a variant recension of U019-U025), the names of the fourth, fifth and octave, the author's δίς names, and the paraphonic/antiphonic consonances. Four decisions matter most. First, σύμφθαρσις is 'fusion' (LSJ, Pape, Bailly), never 'compression'. Second, διαφόρων τόνων means 'several tones'. Third, in U035 the subject is τὸ δι’ ὀκτώ, ἐπαναδιπλουμένων is best 'repeated again' (LSJ), and the δίς names are the author's own term for the intervals recurring after the octave (8:3, 3:1, 4:1). They should be rendered as names with the Greek and a note, not silently as the classical 'double fourth' (16:9, dissonant in Sect. can. 11), and Xylander's emendation is unnecessary. Fourth, κατὰ παράφωνον/ἀντίφωνον follow Thrasyllus in Theon p. 48 H, not Gaudentius. The ῥυθμός of U026 is the one point the editor must decide on interpretation. A and E are the best bases (E slightly ahead in U027, U028, U034, U036; A in U035). D is reliable. B is clean but thin. F is mostly good, with one major slip in U035. C has repeated major errors and false notes and should not serve as a base.
overall.contamination: Met while checking parallels in the archive.org OCR of Jan's Musici scriptores Graeci (1895). None of it was read further or used. (1) A grep for 'δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων' returned one line from Jan's prolegomena (p. 610 reference, '… δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων μουσικῶν τουτέστι δι’ ὀκτώ …'), of unidentified source and possibly a later Byzantine author. (2) A grep for ἄμεσ-/ἔμμεσ- returned one line from Jan's prolegomena quoting 'μὲν οὖν ἔμμεσα' and citing Vincent ('ἰστέον δέ'): evidently a citation of this text's P passages (U042, U050). (3) Jan's footnotes under Cleonides c. 5 (pp. 187-188) cross-refer to Bryennius ('Bryenn. 1, 5'; 'cf. Bry. p. 882') next to a short Greek quotation from Meibom's text; I did not follow them. Nothing forbidden appeared in the LSJ entries consulted (Perseus XML, Logeion: none cites this text) or in Hiller's Theon (text and apparatus pp. 48-56).

checks.note: LSJ s.v. ῥυθμός [checked]: I measured motion/rhythm; II measure, proportion; III arrangement, order; VI manner. A's 'course of the exposition' is in no sense of the entry. Theon p. 52.6-16 H [checked] makes the voice's progression go 'not at random but by defined ways, by which the differences of the genera are seen', which fits 'order' and the promise 'in what follows' (the genera). But U037 makes the author's consonance classes temporal (ἰσοχρόνως/ἀνισοχρόνως, εὐρύθμως), so a temporal 'rhythm' cannot be excluded. Keeping 'rhythm (ῥυθμός)' with a note is the prudent choice. Pape and Bailly were not reopened.
B ru reads «поскольку это позволяет ритм». It turns ὡς ἄν + subjunctive into a cause. Minor.
A search of the whole Greek text confirms that U026 is the first occurrence of ἀσύνθετ-, and B gives no Greek there. Minor.
C en has no Greek at all, and C ru lacks (ἀσύνθετα). Minor.
«триполутоние» is an ad hoc coinage. Minor.

The claim is partly right. LSJ s.v. δίτονος gives δίτονον, the major third, at Aristox. Harm. p. 65 M. [checked]. LSJ cites τριημιτόνιον only from Cleonides and Plutarch, and διτόνιον is not in LSJ [checked]. The Aristoxenus loci in the note are unverified, not shown false.
checks.correction: Minor imprecision, not a false claim. Add that the forms διτόνιον/τριτόνιον are the compiler's; the theorists write δίτονον/τρίτονον (LSJ; Cleonides 5).

checks.note: Barker's standard term is 'incomposite' [from memory]. Minor.

LSJ s.v. σύμφθαρσις [checked]: 'simultaneous destruction' (Alex. Aphr. Mixt. 216.24) and 'melting into one another' (Hermog. Id. 1.12; Iambl. in Nic. p. 80 P.). LSJ s.v. συμφθείρω, passive, of colours 'melt or die away into each other', of sounds D.H. Dem. 48, of π and σ in ψ Comp. 14 [checked]. No lexicon gives 'compression'.
All readings are acceptable. A's and D's 'fusion of three dieses' loses nothing.

LSJ s.v. διάφορος [checked] gives 'several, various' (Phld.; POxy 1033, iv AD; Ep. Hebr. 9.13). In the same text, U014 προσηγορίαι … διάφοροι means 'various names'. 'Several' is best, but 'various' (A) and Russian «разных»/«различных» (= 'various') are legitimate. Only English 'different tones' really suggests tones of unequal size, or even different keys.
checks.correction: The fault is in English 'different' only. The Russian renderings of A, C and F are acceptable.

«воздаваясь» ('being repaid') is nonsense for ἀπηχούμενον. LSJ s.v. ἀπηχέω: 'sound back, re-echo; utter' [checked]. It is probably a slip for «отдаваясь», but as printed the Russian clause is unintelligible. Major for the Russian reader; the English is right.

Theon pp. 54.20-55.4 H [checked]: after two semitones the voice can only make 'the incomposite trihemitonic [interval]' (τὸ τριημιτονιαῖον ἀσύνθετον); in the enharmonic the ditone is the remainder (p. 55.8-10). Cleonides 5 (Jan p. 188) [checked]: the trihemitone is incomposite in the chromatic, the ditone in the enharmonic. These are the intervals left over beside the two small ones, not compressed small steps. Major.

checks.note: Checked: Theon p. 48.16-20 H (σύμφωνα κατ' ἀντίφωνον = διὰ πασῶν, δὶς διὰ πασῶν; κατὰ παράφωνον = διὰ πέντε, διὰ τεσσάρων). Gaudentius 8 (Jan pp. 337-338): παράφωνοι are between consonant and dissonant, the three tones parhypate meson-paramese and the two tones meson diatonos-paramese. LSJ s.vv. ἀντίφωνος III and παράφωνος. [Arist.] Probl. 19.39 (Jan p. 100): the antiphone is the octave, boys and men, as nete to hypate. Theon is plainly this compiler's source here: Theon p. 49.4-5 H, 'ὁ γὰρ τόνος καὶ ἡ δίεσις ἀρχὴ μὲν συμφωνίας, οὔπω δὲ συμφωνία', is U038 almost verbatim.

verify.summary:
The first reviewer's findings are largely sound. The decisive points survive a check against the sources: σύμφθαρσις means 'fusion' (LSJ), never 'compression'. τὸ δι' ὀκτώ is the subject in U035. The δίς names mean the intervals recurring after the octave: Sect. can. 11 calls two fourths dissonant, while Theon and Cleonides use 'octave and fourth/fifth' for 8:3 and 3:1. The paraphonic/antiphonic classes follow Thrasyllus in Theon p. 48 H, not Gaudentius. The compiler plainly draws on Theon here: U038 is Theon p. 49.4-5 almost verbatim.

C's major errors are all confirmed: compression and the pyknon doctrine, «воздаваясь», the false claim that the U027 word is a conjecture, the U031 construal, the U035 inversion, and the false Cleonides 12 / Gaudentius 4 citation. F's major error in U035 is also confirmed.

Corrections:
- U027: διάφορος 'several, various'. The fault is English 'different'; the Russian «разных/различных» is acceptable.
- U031: LSJ's 'reversely' construction of περιτίθημι does not license τετράγωνον αὐτήν, and E leans to a slip for αὐτῇ, not to the accusative construal. The sense is certain either way.
- U034: verb flattening also occurs in C, in D ru and in F en. Bas. reads τελούμενον twice, so the distinction is a minor matter. B's missing etymology hardly matters in U034.
- U035: 'doubled again' is defensible, since it keeps the author's link to δίς. D, E and F all annotate 'double fourth', so the naming question is purely terminological and for the editor.
- Smaller adjustments: C's Aristoxenian-terms note (U026) is partly right; C's checks already give the δίς referents (U035); in U036 the real fault is C's bracket around [интервал] for the transmitted διάστασις.

Missed: three minor faults (F 'trisemitone', U026; C «там же», U029; C's same verb for τελούμενον and τελειούμενον, U034). No best_ru/best_en choice needs changing. Pape and Bailly were not reopened. The ῥυθμός question (U026) stays with the editor: 'rhythm' with a note is the prudent rendering.

units.sense: Paraphonic and antiphonic [consonance] differ in that the paraphonic is consonant 'at unequal times' (ἀνισοχρόνως), the notes taking turns with one another somewhat gently and rhythmically, in proportions and ratios, evenly. The antiphonic is consonant 'at equal times', the high note sounding with the low at the same time (κατὰ ταὐτόν): note 8 with 1, 11 with 4, 12 with 5, 15 with 8, all octave pairs of U014. The low notes rise or fall together with the high (or the high with the low) proportionally in raisings or lowerings. The time criterion is the compiler's own: Thrasyllus in Theon 48.16-49.2 Hiller explains the two classes differently.

divergences.verdict: The text glosses ἰσοχρόνως itself with κατὰ ταὐτόν ('at the same time') and describes paraphony as the notes 'taking turns' (διαδεχομένων ἀλλήλοις). So the contrast is about when the sounds occur, perhaps coloured by the 'motions' theory of Probl. XIX.39 (εὐρύθμως; λόγον κινήσεως). LSJ's 'of unequal duration' (Herodicus; metric) would make note length the criterion; nothing in the context supports that, and D's 'durations' then sits awkwardly beside its own 'at the same time'. The literal 'at unequal/equal times' keeps the source's ambiguity. B's explicit simultaneity is an acceptable interpretation. E's calque is correct but opaque in Russian.

units.sense: The fourth is made up of two tones and a semitone 'and a little something besides' (πρός adverbial). Being smaller even than a diesis, this has received no name. The fifth is three [tones] and a semitone; the octave 'through' six [tones]; 'the octave and double fourth' eight and a semitone; 'the octave and double fifth' nine and a semitone; the double octave twelve. These are the school's additive figures (Cleonides p. 194; Gaudentius c. 10, p. 339). In Pythagorean ratios the surplus has the wrong sign (Sect. can. 15). It probably comes from Theon's report that Plato's fourth is two tones plus the 'so-called leimma', which is ἀκατονόμαστον (nameless): the compiler added this nameless remainder to Aristoxenus' 2½ tones. The δίς names conflate the standard 'octave and fourth/fifth' with the author's own 'double fourth/fifth' (= 11th, 12th; U035). The tone counts show that the 11th and 12th are meant.

units.sense: It must be observed that the mediate intervals (those with intermediate notes) have their ratios referred to the proslambanomenos. These are the fourth, the fifth (with the obscure μέλος), the octave, the double fourth, the double fifth and the double octave. The immediate intervals lying between them (diesis, semitone, tone) have their particular ratio-relation to the near notes before them. And [it must be observed] also how intervals enlarged by the fusion of several intervals (tridiesis, trihemitone, ditone, tritone and the like) are thus blended into one interval, as by fusion, once the intervals hidden in them have first been assigned ratios to the near notes. Cleonides (Jan p. 194) likewise measures all six consonances from proslambanomenos.

units.sense: So then the intervals of music too are thus disposed as regards their ratios (or: so it is with the ratios and the intervals of music). The ratio of the mediate intervals is compared, by overstepping, with the extreme notes; that of the immediate ones successively with the notes near one another. The increase from the smaller to the greater [terms] proceeds in series, and no unit is divided, since not even the arithmeticians accept this. The singular τοῦ with the plural συγκρινομένων is best explained as attraction to τῶν ἀμέσων.

That is, they are judged by pitch, not by the count of positions; U046-U047 develop the point. The text prints ἢ (H Par. V P); Bas. has οὐ.

by_translator.strengths: Accurate and literal. Construal is careful, e.g. the dependent ὡς-clause in U042. Greek is given at first occurrences. References checked by the reviewer were right: Theon 48-49, 53, Sect. can. on Jan p. 161, Nicomachus Ench. 6 on Jan p. 248. Doubts are sound and the text_issues balanced.
by_translator.weaknesses: The Russian is over-literal in places ('в ровности', 'идёт рядом', 'имеют отнесение'). Literal ordinals in U041 collide with the note numbers of U037. 'Усиление' for ἐπίτασις suggests loudness. A Russian note glosses ἐπιμερής as 'сверхчастное'. 'The fifth melody' is ambiguous. In U039 A floats an emendation that is not needed.

by_translator.strengths: Readable versions with the sense mostly right; the doubts on δίς are reasonable.
by_translator.weaknesses: Thin doctrine and notes. Greek terms are almost never given at first occurrences. 'Согласуется' for συμφωνεῖν. In U043 the Russian 'через промежуточные' reverses καθ’ ὑπερβατόν. ὡς ἐπὶ ὑποδείγματος is omitted in U041. The causal participle is flattened in U039. Inaccurate text_issues report for U040.

by_translator.strengths: The English is mostly accurate. Arithmetic checks are good (U039, U041). The text issue on the missing 4:1 is reasonable.
by_translator.weaknesses: Major Russian errors: ἔμμεσα rendered 'мелодические' in U042-U044, and σύμφθαρσις as 'сжатие/compression' in both languages. The calqued interval names ('через четыре', 'через все') make the Russian hard to read and partly ungrammatical. In U037, 'кротко ... стройно' and 'антифон' mislead. δέδοκται is misread. Wrong Sectio canonis pages and a non-existent leimma reference; the note on the surplus ignores the sign.

by_translator.strengths: Careful and explicit, with good doubts. Correct descriptive Russian ratio terms. The construal of U044's opening and the treatment of συγκρινομένων are good. Cleonides p. 194 is cited correctly.
by_translator.weaknesses: 'Durations' for ἀνισοχρόνως imposes note length. Digit errors in the U039 checks. ὡς ἐπὶ ὑποδείγματος is omitted in U041. Some interpretive expansions ('с промежуточными звуками') and anachronistic acoustic caveats.

by_translator.strengths: The best documented. Verified parallels: Theon 56-57 and 67, Probl. XIX.18 and 39, Gaudentius 8, DGE/Anon. Bellermann. Standard Russian ratio terms (сверхмногочастное). Good apparatus notes and construal. An insightful, explicitly labelled hypothesis on the surplus in U039.
by_translator.weaknesses: Wrong Theon page in U038 (p. 50 for p. 49). 'Усиление/intensification' for ἐπίτασις. The calque 'неизохронно'. 'Следует же рассмотреть, что'. The claim that the leimma is 'named' conflicts with Theon's ἀκατονόμαστον. The U036 note (a context unit) relies on a Jan editorial note that itself quotes this text.

by_translator.strengths: The clearest and most idiomatic Russian and English, with accurate construal throughout. Correct pitch sense of τάσις/ἄνεσις and ἐπίτασις. Precise checks and notes.
by_translator.weaknesses: 'Сверхчастное' for ἐπιμερής in U040-U041 (a major term error). 'The fifth melody' is ambiguous. Fewer source parallels.

overall.summary:
Group 3 (U037-U045): the antiphonic/paraphonic distinction, the tone counts and ratios of the six consonances, the base-6 example, the Paris-only passage on mediate and immediate intervals (U042-U044), and the principle that ratios follow pitch.

All six translators read the printed text as printed and keep the edition signs correctly: ⟨⟨ opens U042 and ⟩⟩ closes U044.

Real errors:
- C: two major mistranslations, ἔμμεσα as 'мелодические' and σύμφθαρσις as 'compression'.
- F: 'сверхчастное' for διπλασιεπιμερής.
- B: a reversed Russian rendering of καθ’ ὑπερβατόν.

Divergences for the editor:
- ἀνισοχρόνως: recommend the literal 'at unequal times'.
- δίς in the compound names: keep. All witnesses have it at 29.8-9 and H has it at 29.14-15; it is the compiler's conflation with his own names.
- The surplus καὶ μικρόν τι πρός: keep, and explain it. Theon 67.9-15, which no translator cites for this, calls Plato's leimma ἀκατονόμαστον; this is the probable source of 'received no name'. The compiler's surplus is then Plato's nameless remainder added to Aristoxenus' 2½ tones.
- The missing 4:1 in U040: keep the printed text and note it.
- μέλος in U042: keep, with a note.
- The construal of the opening of U044.

On balance, E and F give the best bases (E for documentation and terms, F for style). A is a reliable literal control. D is careful but sometimes over-interprets. B is thin. C's Russian needs heavy revision in U042-U044.
overall.contamination:
Met by accident and not used:
(1) Jan, Musici scriptores Graeci p. 338, the editorial note to Gaudentius c. 8 on παράφωνοι, quotes 'Psellus mus. p. 28', i.e. the opening words of U036, together with Meibom's proposed insertion of 'octave and fourth / octave and fifth'. It surfaced in a text dump while I was reading Gaudentius c. 8-10; I stopped reading it.
(2) Hiller's apparatus to Theon p. 53.1 cites 'Bryenn. p. 396' for a variant in Theon's own text.

verify.summary:
I checked every finding for U037-U045. Most stand. The changes that matter:

1. The surplus in U039 (μικρόν τι πρός). Keeping it unemended is right, but tracing it to Theon 67 is overstated. In Theon, ἀκατονόμαστον describes the leimma's ratio, not its name: the interval is 'the so-called leimma'. The leimma also replaces the semitone and is larger than the text's own diesis (33:32), so it cannot be the remainder 'smaller even than a diesis'. Theon 67 is at most a possible echo of 'received no name'. For the same reason, the error claimed against E's 'the Pythagoreans name it λεῖμμα' is rejected.

2. Two of the reviewer's source claims are wrong. Cleonides p. 194 measures only five consonances from proslambanomenos (the fourth runs hypate hypaton to hypate meson). Theon's base-6 series has no 16: he shows 8:3 as 3:4:8. The exact 16:6 parallel is Nicomachus, Ar. I 23.3.

3. Real errors confirmed:
- C: ἔμμεσα rendered 'мелодические' (one error repeated in U042-U044); σύμφθαρσις rendered 'compression' (LSJ, Bailly and Pape all give fusion).
- F: 'сверхчастное' for διπλασιεπιμερής. In Shchetnikov's Russian Nicomachus that term means ἐπιμόριον, so F names the wrong class. It is one error across U040-U041, not two majors.
- D: wrong tone figures in the U039 checks.
- E: Theon page (p. 50 for 49.2-4).
- C: wrong Sectio canonis pages.

4. Findings softened:
- D's 'durations' is the lexicon's first sense: interpretive, and it does not clash with D's 'at the same time'.
- C's 'стройно' is within εὔρυθμος.
- A's literal ordinals are accurate and explained in a note.
- B's 'через' in U043 is ambiguous, not reversed (minor).
- The U044 construal is a tie between two grammatical parses, not an edge for D.

5. Citation fixes: Gaudentius is c. 1 (p. 328), not c. 2. Best Russian for U039 should be F; best English E = F.

No major errors were missed. Two minor ones are listed.

units.sense: For the interval of the fifth, though it has the hemiolic ratio (3:2), does not appear hemiolic by the excess in the number of notes it has when compared with the notes before it. Compared with the first note it is found to be fivefold, with the second double-and-a-half, with the third superbipartient (5:3), with the fourth sesquiquartan (5:4), and against none is it shown to be hemiolic. (The masculine συγκρινόμενος/ἡμιόλιος shift to the implied fifth note.)

units.sense: Such ratios of the intervals have been found from the difference in the length of the strings, or in their thickness, or in the tension produced by turning the pegs (κόλλαβοι), or, more familiarly, from the hanging of weights. On wind instruments they have been found either from the width of the bores (κοιλίαι) or from the tightening and slackening of the breath. (Almost verbatim from Theon 56.19–57.6 H.)

divergences.greek: ἢ γνωριμώτερον ἀπὸ τῆς ἐξαρτήσεως τῶν βαρῶν
divergences.issue: Sense of γνωριμώτερον

readings.en: or, more familiarly, from the hanging of weights
readings.ru: или, что более привычно/известно, из подвешивания грузов

readings.en: or, more clearly, from the suspension of weights
readings.ru: или, более наглядно (ещё нагляднее), по подвешиванию грузов

divergences.verdict: LSJ γνώριμος gives 'well-known, familiar'; the comparative means 'more knowable/intelligible' (Aristotle), and the adverb means 'intelligibly'. Both senses exist, but the source phrase in Theon 57.3 and Theon's own usage (ἐπὶ τὸ γνωριμώτερον, 47.12) favour 'more familiar / more intelligibly'. The weights are the well-known legendary route. 'Нагляднее' (more visually) adds an idea not in the word.
evidence: Theon ed. Hiller 57.2-3 (ἢ γνωριμώτερον κατὰ τὴν ἐξάρτησιν τῶν βαρῶν) and 47.12 [checked]
divergences.recommended_en: or, more familiarly, from the hanging of weights
divergences.recommended_ru: или, что более известно, по подвешиванию грузов

errors.quote: Boethius ... (who adds that the weight experiment in fact fails to produce the ratios)
errors.problem: False. Boethius, Inst. mus. 1.11 (Friedlein p. 198) reports that Pythagoras tested the ratios with weights, pipes and cups and was glad to find 'nihil sese diversum'. There is no reservation there; criticism of such experiments is Ptolemaic (Harm. 1.8) [Boethius checked; Ptolemy from memory].
errors.fix: Delete the parenthesis, or replace it with: 'Ptolemy (Harm. 1.8) criticises experiments with weights and pipes as imprecise'.

errors.quote: (ἔμπνευστα)
errors.problem: Wrong accent and breathing in the Greek quoted in the translation.

best_ru.why: Exact; gives the Greek of the rare technical words (κόλλαβοι, ἐξάρτησις, ἐμπνευστά, κοιλίαι) at first occurrence; renders γνωριμώτερον well.

best_en.why: Exact; 'more familiarly' matches the source; 'bores/hollows' is correct.

notes_to_keep.gist: The sentence is almost verbatim Theon 57.1-6 H (Greek quoted; verified); κόλλαβοι in Nicomachus Ench. 6 (Jan 248: τὴν τῶν κολλάβων ... περιστροφήν, verified); cf. Theon 66.5-10 on wind instruments (verified).

Theon adds 'volumes and weights, such as discs or vessels' (δι' ὄγκων καὶ σταθμῶν οἷον δίσκων ἢ ἀγγείων), which the compiler omits; P's variants (τῶν αὐλῶν ἢ τῶν τρημάτων ἀφορότητος; τάσεως; om. καὶ ἀνέσεως).
Physics: a string's frequency goes as √T, so the octave needs a 4:1 weight ratio, not 2:1; the weight legend cannot give the stated ratios (one such note suffices; A, B, E, F say the same).

units.sense: ⟨⟨P only.⟩⟩ One must know that, with tension or with suspension [of weights], greater tightening and greater weight produce the melody towards the high. But with the thickness of the strings, or their length or [that] of the auloi, or the διάτασις of the holes, an excess in any of these makes †ἀμφότερον† (required sense: the lower / the other) species of melody.

divergences.issue: Rendering of the obelized word, and which conjecture to prefer in the note

readings.construal: 'twofold' as an approximation of the corrupt word

divergences.verdict: Both renderings are acceptable inside daggers; the literal '†both†' best shows that the word is corrupt. The sense required is certainly 'lower', and Theon gives the doctrine and the vocabulary. In Theon 65.12–66.10 H the greater weight gives the higher note (τὸ πλεῖον βάρος ... τὸν ὀξύτερον ποιήσει φθόγγον), while lengths and thicknesses make strings sluggish. On wind instruments 'the lower notes' (οἱ βαρύτεροι) come διὰ τὸ μῆκος καὶ τὴν εὐρύτητα τῶν τρημάτων. That favours βαρύτερον for the sense. θάτερον suits the μέν/δέ antithesis and the singular εἶδος. ἀμβλύτερον is closest in letters. The edition rightly obelizes.
evidence: Aristotle, De anima 2.8 420a29-b4 (ὀξύ / ἀμβλύ as tactile analogues of high / low) [from memory]
divergences.recommended_en: the excess of any one of these constitutes †both† species of melody [sense required: the lower]
divergences.recommended_ru: избыток чего-либо из этого образует †и то и другое† (†оба†) вид мелодии [по смыслу: более низкий]

divergences.issue: 'Spacing (distance) of the holes' or 'widening/extension of the holes'

readings.construal: spacing/distance of the holes (E: from the mouthpiece)
readings.ru: расстановки / расстояния между отверстиями / отстояния отверстий

divergences.verdict: Not settled. LSJ gives διάτασις as 'tension, dilatation, extension, stretching across', with no 'spacing' sense attested. Theon 66.5-9 names τὴν εὐρύτητα τῶν τρημάτων (width) as a cause of lower notes, which supports 'widening'. 'Extension' (length to the hole) also gives 'lower'. Recommend the neutral 'extension' with a note on both senses.
evidence: LSJ s.v. διάτασις; Bailly s.v. 'distension, dilatation; extension, allongement' [checked]
P's variant at U049 ἀπὸ τῆς τῶν αὐλῶν ἢ τῶν τρημάτων ἀφορότητος (apparatus Bas. 30.21-22) [checked]
divergences.recommended_en: or the extension (διάτασις) of the holes
divergences.recommended_ru: или протяжённости (διάτασις) отверстий

notes_to_keep.gist: βαρύτης here is the weight of the hung load (a play on βαρύτης 'lowness'); the direction table (more tension or weight → higher; more thickness or length, of strings and pipes → lower); cf. Theon 66.5-10.
Apparatus: ἐξαρτήσεως is Vincent's correction of P's ἐξαντήσεων; ἐργάζεται P (Vinc. dub. ἐξάγεται). The case for θάτερον and ἀμβλύτερον.
Doubt on διάτασις: spacing vs widening of the holes.

διάτασις τῶν τρημάτων: 'spacing', 'widening' or neutral 'extension'?

units.sense: Of the systems, one is the tetrachord, which contains all the powers of the fourth; another the pentachord, which encompasses the powers of the ⟨διά⟩ pente (fifth); another the octachord, which contains the whole force of the octave. Another is the sixteen-chord by continuity, which holds together the entire extent of the double octave and has its powers doubled: for it contains in itself both the aforesaid [powers] and those of the double fourth, the double fifth and the double octave. (In the author's usage, U035, 'double fourth/fifth' are the octave-compounds 8:3 and 3:1.)

divergences.issue: How to keep the edition sign when διὰ πέντε is normally rendered by one word

readings.construal: 'fifth' unmarked in the translation; sign kept in the Greek parenthesis
readings.en: the powers of the fifth (⟨dia⟩ pente)

readings.construal: the whole word 'fifth' in angle brackets, explained in a note
literal, with exact scope of the sign
literal; ru exact, en brackets the wrong word

divergences.verdict: The sign must cover only the supplied διά. B, D and F do this exactly. A and E are workable compromises (A marks the Greek, E explains in a note), but neither marks exactly what was supplied. C's English marks the transmitted 'five' as supplied, which is wrong. The convention is the editor's.

divergences.issue: What 'double fourth/fifth' denotes

readings.construal: literal names kept; text_issues say the intended referents are octave+fourth and octave+fifth, F hedging that literal 16:9 and 9:4 may also fit

divergences.verdict: Keep the literal names in the translation. The author defines them himself in U035: the intervals after the octave 'are called' double fourth, double fifth, double octave. U037 gives the 11th against the 4th note and the 12th against the 5th, and U040–U041 the ratios 8:3 and 3:1. So the sense is 8:3 and 3:1, not 16:9 and 9:4, and F's hedge has no support. Theon 56.11-16 gives διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ τεσσάρων 8:3 and διὰ πασῶν καὶ διὰ πέντε 3:1.
evidence: U035, U037, U040-U041 of this text [checked]

notes_to_keep.gist: The printed συστημάτων rests on P alone; Bas. H Par. V read διαστημάτων ('of the intervals'). U052 supports 'systems'.
Adrastus in Theon 49.13-16 H: the systems (tetrachords, pentachords, octachords) are the ὁλοσχερῆ parts of all melody (verified).

The examples are Thrasyllus' (Theon 48.10-11 H: σύστημα ... οἷον τετράχορδον, πεντάχορδον, ὀκτάχορδον; verified). δύναμις here is 'power, capacity', not the Aristoxenian note-function; apparatus ἐμπεριέχον, ὅλην, διάστασιν.

Should the note record that συστημάτων is P's reading against διαστημάτων of all other witnesses?

units.sense: Systems differ from the intervals in between [their notes] in that systems have their constitution in matter, whereas intervals are conceived by abstraction from matter.

units.sense: It is proper to harmonia to arrange and fit together such systems for such-and-such a genus of melody: the diatonic, the chromatic, and the one called 'harmonic', paronymously from harmonia itself.

The name is attested: Theon's diagram 56 H has δίεσις δίεσις δίτονον ἁρμονικόν; Gaudentius 5 has ἐν μὲν τῷ ἁρμονικῷ τὸ πρῶτον ... διάστημα τέταρτον τόνου; Cleonides calls the genus ἁρμονία.

Naz.) and (b) funeral, funeral procession = ἐκφορά; ἐξοδιακός 'pertaining to burial'; τὸ ἐξοδιαστικόν 'the burial service'. by_translator.strengths: Exact, literal, complete. Identifies the direct source, Theon of Smyrna, for U049, U054 and U057–U064, quotes it accurately, and links U051 and U065 to Adrastus and Thrasyllus in Theon 48–49. The LSJ citations hold, including the true observation that Perseus's LSJ reads '4:3' s.v. ἐπιτέταρτος. Good doubts on γνωριμώτερον, κοινὴ ἁρμονία and ἐξόδιος. Sound text_issues.
by_translator.weaknesses: Rendering μελῳδία as «мелодика» produces unidiomatic plurals («видов мелодик»). Some archaisms («многой упражнённости») and a typo («теченями»). Misconstrues συντακτικῷ in U062. The note on U059 glosses παρατετράφθαι as 'coloured'. Little Greek in parentheses for the new ratio names in U046.

by_translator.strengths: Clear, readable Russian and English, generally right in sense; a sensible note on the participle in U058; the singular εἶδος problem noted in U050.
by_translator.weaknesses: Very thin apparatus: almost no Greek at first occurrences (ratio names, genera), so the technical terms are dissolved into paraphrase. Omissions in U051 (γάρ; 'the powers of'). Misleading «исходная песнь» in U065. 'Transposition' and 'pauses' in U066. κρίνεται rendered 'is called' in U047. διάστασις inconsistent within the group. A note and the translation disagree on διάτασις in U050.

by_translator.strengths: Consistently literal system ('through four' and so on). Usually correct arithmetic checks. Sees that the fourth's remainder is strictly the leimma.
by_translator.weaknesses: Normalizes the author's ἁρμονικόν to 'enharmonic' (U053, U054, U060, U063), against about.md §4 and the stated paronymy. Renders σύμφθαρσις as 'compression' (U058, U060). A false claim about Boethius 1.10–11 (U049). Misconstruals in U046 (πρός), U050 ('[каналов]'), U052 and U055. Coinages and unidiomatic Russian («мелопения», «составительный», «завершаемый из», 'super-quartient'). Misplaces ⟨ ⟩ in the English of U051. Some loose reference loci.

by_translator.strengths: The most attentive to the apparatus: alone notes that the printed συστημάτων in U051 rests on P against all other witnesses. Good doubts (διάτασις, ἀμφότερον, συγκεκραμένον); careful physics and cents. Verified parallels (Gaudentius 5 for ἁρμονικόν). Exact scope of ⟨ ⟩.
by_translator.weaknesses: Some paraphrase in place of translation (U046 '[номера] звука'). Doublet and inconsistent renderings of the -chord terms in U051. Elative for the superlative in U063. Vague «с прибавлением двух долей» for ἐπιδιμερής. 'Farewell song' for ἐξόδιος. Some notes over-hedged.

by_translator.strengths: The best overall. Exact translations with the Greek at first occurrences; distinguishes μέλος («мелос») from μελῳδία; finest choices (διαμοναί 'sustainings', «отыменно» for παρωνύμως, etymological οὕτω). Systematically traces the compiler's adaptations of Theon (omissions of discs and vessels, of φιλότεχνον; τριβή added; φυσικώτερον). The fullest apparatus notes. The best doubts (ἐξόδιος funeral triad, κοινὴ ἁρμονία, θάτερον/ἀμβλύτερον).
by_translator.weaknesses: Several Theon page references are off (p. 53 for 54.7-14; 53-54 for 55.4-6). '⟨квинты⟩/⟨fifth⟩' extends the angle brackets over the transmitted word (explained in a note). Occasionally plural «оба вида» for the singular εἶδος (U050).

by_translator.strengths: Exact handling of the edition signs; clear checks and diagrams (Pythagorean realizations); good explanatory notes on συγκεκραμένον and on the additive scheme versus the leimma.
by_translator.weaknesses: Notes often cite only 'greek-text.json' or a physics textbook instead of the theorists. Theon is never identified as the source. Hedges, without support, that 'double fourth/fifth' might be literal (16:9, 9:4) despite U035. Wrong accent in (ἔμπνευστα); a dangling «оно» (U047); nonstandard 'trisemitone'; διάστασις inconsistent in English.

overall.summary:
All six translations are usable and agree on the sense of most units. The decisive points of this group:

- U049–U064 follow Theon of Smyrna almost word for word (Hiller 54.6–57.6, 65.12–66.10); A and E show this and it should go into the commentary.
- ἁρμονικόν must stay 'harmonic'. It is attested in Theon's diagram and in Gaudentius 5, and the paronymy is the author's own point. C's 'enharmonic' is a major fault, as is C's 'compression' for σύμφθαρσις.
- U050: the sense 'lower' for the crux †ἀμφότερον† is certain, from the parallel at Theon 65–66. The choice of conjecture, and the meaning of διάτασις τῶν τρημάτων ('spacing' against the lexically better 'dilatation/extension'), are the editor's.
- U051: the printed συστημάτων is P's reading against διαστημάτων of all other witnesses (noted only by D). The convention for marking ⟨διὰ⟩ πέντε needs to be fixed.
- U060 κοινὴ ἁρμονία and U065 ἐξόδιος are open. Sophocles' Lexicon attests the Byzantine sense 'funeral' for τὸ ἐξόδιον.

Best bases: E for most units in both languages, A close behind. D for textual notes.
overall.contamination: I met no citation of this text. While reading permitted editions I met three citations of forbidden later authors, none about this text. (1) In the First1KGreek file of Hiller's Theon, Hiller's apparatus on p. 49 (line 10) cites a variant of Theon's text from 'Manuel Bryennius p. 393'. (2) In the archive.org OCR of Jan's Musici scriptores Graeci, the note of parallels at Cleonides c. 2 (Jan p. 180/181) cites 'Manuel Bryenn. harm. I 3'. (3) A codex description in Jan's prolegomena mentions manuscripts of 'Bryenni libri I et II'. I stopped reading at each and used none of them. verify.summary:
The first reviewer's findings largely hold.

**Confirmed major faults, all translator C**
- C normalizes ἁρμονικόν to 'enharmonic' (U053, U054, U060, U063).
- C renders σύμφθαρσις as 'compression' (U058, U060).
- C's note says Boethius reports that the weight experiment fails. Friedlein p. 198 says the opposite.
- The first two are systematic choices and should each be weighed once.

**Corrections**
- **U049 γνωριμώτερον:** the evidence does not favour 'more familiarly'. LSJ glosses the adverb as 'intelligibly', and Theon himself uses the word for 'more clearly' (47.12, 49.6). 'More clearly' and «нагляднее» (translators B, C, D, F) are at least as good, and no translator is at fault.
- **U050 διάτασις:** no lexicon gives 'spacing'. That sense needs διάστασις, a confusion attested in this tradition at Bas. 31.5. Translator B's 'widening', backed by Theon 66.6-8, is the lexically sound rendering of the printed word. The majority render 'spacing' without flagging it.
- **U050 τῶν αὐλῶν:** translator C's [каналов] follows the majority construal with a superfluous supplement, and an ἐπί-construal is also possible.
- **U046:** translator D's 'by two parts' for ἐπιδιμερής is a literal calque (Nicomachus says thirds are understood), not a mistranslation.
- **U065 ἐξόδιος:** the funeral sense is attested for τὸ ἐξόδιον, not for the adjective, and translator D's 'departure song' is defensible.
- **U047:** translator F's «оно» can refer back to «отношение».
- **U049:** translator F's ἔμπνευστα is an accent error only; the breathing is correct.
- **U055:** translator C's fault is the verb «излагается», not τὸ πᾶν.
- **U051:** the recommended rendering should not put ratios into the translation, since the brief keeps them in notes.

**Missed by the first reviewer:** only minor points (listed above).

An excerpt from Macran's Aristoxenus showed a few lines of his apparatus (variants; Bellermann; the Anonymus Bellermanni), which are not forbidden. The testimonia line in Hoche's Nicomachus names Philoponus, Iamblichus and Boethius. The Sophocles, LSJ, DGE, Bailly and Pape entries I opened do not cite this text. Russian should therefore use the same adjective as the genus (recommended «диатонический»), as a feminine substantive that agrees with the printed feminine διεζευγμένη. A and F's masculine-looking «диатонос» with «отделённая» is a gender clash. C's «диатон» is Shchetnikov's form for this note, but «диатон» also names the diatonic genus in the Aleksandrova-Myakin school. English should transliterate like every other note name; B and C's 'diatonic [note] of ...' mixes systems inside one list. Do not normalize ὑπάτη διάτονος to 'lichanos hypaton' in the text; a note can give the standard name. The edition's word order ⟨μέσων διάτονος⟩ matches Nicomachus' list.

terms.why: The author treats the three as one series (U035), and «двойная октава / double octave» is standard. A note is needed at U035/U036. Here δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων is octave + fourth (8:3) and δὶς διὰ πέντε is octave + fifth (3:1): the fourth and fifth 'repeated' in the second octave (U035 ἐπαναδιπλουμένων). They are not two fourths (16:9, dissonant in the Sectio canonis) or two fifths (9:4). Xylander's conjectures are not printed.

terms.recommended_en: concord; be concordant (alternative: consonance; be consonant)
terms.why: The schools differ. Tsypin uses «консонанс». The Russian translations of Nicomachus (Shchetnikov, Aleksandrova-Myakin) render συμφωνία as «созвучие», but in modern Russian «созвучие» means any simultaneity, so «консонанс» is more exact. A, B and C, which use «созвучн-/согласоваться» for the verb and «консонанс» for the noun, break the link. Barker's English is 'concord/concordant', with 'discordant' kept for διάφωνος; all six chose 'consonance'.
evidence: Barker, GMW II: concord / concordant; discord / discordant [from memory]

terms.greek: τὸ παράφωνον / τὸ ἀντίφωνον; κατὰ παράφωνον / κατὰ ἀντίφωνον
terms.why: The Greek is a substantivized neuter adjective and an adverbial κατά-phrase. Russian «антифония» (alternate choral singing) and «антифон» (a liturgical chant) mislead, and so do English 'antiphony/antiphonal'. The Anonymous's class members are Thrasyllus' (octave and double octave κατ' ἀντίφωνον; fifth and fourth κατὰ παράφωνον). Gaudentius' different sense of παράφωνοι must not be imported.
evidence: LSJ s.v. ἀντίφωνος: concordant, as in the octave; τὸ ἀντίφωνον concord in the octave, Arist. Pr. 918b30 [checked]
LSJ s.v. παράφωνος: in Gaud. Harm. 8 sounds midway between consonance and dissonance, e.g. the tritone [checked]

terms.why: The ratio names need one system per language. Shchetnikov's calques (Nicomachus) are the only published Russian set that covers every ratio in this text. Both Russian schools use «полуторное», which is also an exact calque. A and C's transliterations are isolated. In English, 'hemiolic' is Barker's term.

terms.why: Use one pattern, which also feeds the compounds («двукратное с половиной», «двукратно-сверхмногочастное»). This is Shchetnikov's usage. πενταπλασίων = πενταπλάσιος. Keep the geometric διπλασιάζω (U023-U031) as «удвоить/double».

Theon calls 8:3 a πολλαπλασιεπιμερής ratio, 'double and bi-epitritic'. The Anonymous fuses 'double' with the generic class name ἐπιμερής, superpartient (1 + m/n). F's «сверхчастное» and C's «надчастное» name the superparticular (ἐπιμόριος) class, which is wrong for 2 + 2/3. B's «с долями» is vague. Shchetnikov's class terms are «сверхмногочастное» and «многократно-и-сверхмногочастное». Barker's English is 'epimeric'.

terms.why: In the definition, which comes from Thrasyllus, τάσις is the pitch on which a voice rests. In U049-U050 it is the string's physical tension from the pegs; in U037, paired with ἀνέσεσι, it means tightenings. Two epimoric ratios, 4:3 and 5:4, are named by different systems. The English is mixed in the same way ('epitritic, epitetartic' but 'superbipartient, double-superpartient').

In Russian, «гипата диатонная» (an adjective) but «диатонос средних / отделённая / высших» (a transliterated noun) for the same Greek word in one list. «диатонос отделённая» joins a masculine-looking noun to feminine agreement.

Transliteration for ἐπίτριτος, ἐπιτέταρτος and ἐπόγδοος («эпитритное», «эпитетартное», «эпогдоическое») but calques for ἐπιδιμερής («сверхдвухчастное») and διπλασιεπιμερής («двойное сверхчастное»). «величина/magnitude» (U027) but «возможности/capacities» (U051). This is intentional by F's list, but it loses U027's contrast between potential and actual sound.

«восьмиструнник / eight-string system» (U015, U035) but «октахорд / octachord» (U051).

τάσις is «высота» (U008), «повышение» (U037) and «натяжение» (U049, U050); ἐπίτασις is «повышение» (U045, U047), «усиление» (U049) and «натяжение» (U050). In U050 the same Russian word stands for τάσις and ἐπίτασις, and ἄνεσις is «понижение» (U037) but «ослабление» (U049).

terms.summary:
The six translators agree on most of the basic vocabulary: note, interval, system, diesis, semitone, tone, tridiesis, ditone, tritone, incomposite, the standard note names, genus, chromatic, the geometric terms and the experiment terms (much of which the text takes verbatim from Theon). The real divergences fall in five areas.

1. Ratio names. No translator except A (Greek-based) and D (descriptive Russian) uses one system. C, E and F mix transliteration and calque within the same family, and C and F misclassify 8:3 (and C also 5:4) as superparticular. I recommend Barker-style Greek-based terms in English (epitritic, hemiolic, epogdoic, double-epimeric, epidimeric, epitetartic). In Russian I recommend Shchetnikov's published calques (полуторное, сверхтретье, сверхвосьмерное, сверхдвухчастное, сверхчетвертное, двукратное с половиной, двукратно-сверхмногочастное), with the Aleksandrova-Myakin transliterations as the alternative; the editor should choose.

2. The τάσις / ἐπίτασις / ἄνεσις cluster. The translators split 3:3 between 'pitch' and 'tension' at U008, and B, D and F use one Russian word for τάσις and ἐπίτασις in U050.

3. The note names. The printed by-forms (διάτονος as a note name, παράμεσος, singular διεζευγμένη) are treated in five different ways; Nicomachus Ench. 11-12 supports keeping them.

4. The text's own terms. ἁρμονικόν (keep 'harmonic', against C's 'enharmonic'), σύμφθαρσις (keep 'fusion', against C's 'compression') and δὶς διὰ τεσσάρων (a note is needed: here octave + fourth, not the dissonant 16:9 of the Sectio canonis).

5. Concord against consonance. Barker has 'concord'; all six have 'consonance'. In Russian, «консонанс» (Tsypin) stands against «созвучие» (D and both Russian Nicomachus translations).

Of the translators, E is the most consistent overall, except in its Russian ratio names. D is consistent but descriptive in Russian. A is consistent but keeps literal 'twice-' and ordinal-number forms. B and F vary within units. C departs most from the field (literal 'through four / through all', «мелодические» for ἔμμεσος, 'compression', 'enharmonic', harmony/harmonia split). The editor should first fix the Russian and English ratio systems, the τάσις cluster, the policy for the by-form note names, and concord against consonance; the remaining items follow from those decisions.
terms.contamination:
No forbidden material was read or used.

Precautions:
- First1KGreek texts. I searched Theon (Hiller), Nicomachus' Ench. and Intr. arith. (Jan, Hoche), the Sectio canonis (Menge) and Aristoxenus (Macran) only after a script removed every editorial footnote unread. In Theon I searched only pp. 40-80, never the end of the volume (Hiller's Epilogus).
- I did not open Jan's printed volume, Gaudentius, Bacchius, Meibom, Wallis or Düring.
- Lexica. I read LSJ (Perseus XML) entries and none cited this text. In Sophocles' Lexicon (archive.org OCR) a search for 'Psell' hit only the list of abbreviations ('Psell. — Michael Psellus (A.D. 1050), PG 122'): a general author entry, not a citation of this text. Not used.
- Russian ΣΧΟΛΗ PDFs (classics.nsu.ru). Before reading I ran a token-only check for forbidden names. Aleksandrova's 2009 article (ΣΧΟΛΗ 3.1) mentions Bryennius twice ('Bryenn', 'Вриенн') and contains the word «аноним»; Dillon's preface contains «аноним» once. I filtered out every passage containing those tokens and read none of them. I used only these sources' renderings of Nicomachus' own terms.

Other:
- I did not open A's cited 'Theon, Epilogus diagram'.
- One background grep over the Russian files (with the Bryennius tokens filtered out) wrote its output to a task file that I did not read.
- No web search named this text or its wording.
- The environment contained git and memory notes about tools; I ignored them and they played no part.
